questions.question: Which language should the REE Forma frontend use?
questions.rationale: A typed frontend is a conservative default for a multi-workflow clinic application.

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Typed JavaScript for a maintainable clinic interface.

questions.question: Which frontend framework should be used?
questions.rationale: React with Fluent UI v9 provides a mature, accessible component system for dense operational workflows.

options.label: React
options.description: Component-based UI; use Fluent UI v9 for accessible controls.

options.label: Angular
options.description: Structured TypeScript framework; use Angular Material.

questions.question: What must the frontend support?
questions.answer: Responsive authenticated staff application for patient records, appointment calendar, reminders, assessments, treatment plans, packages, billing, PDF documents, reports, and search; expose controls only when the signed-in user's permissions allow them.
questions.rationale: Directly reflects the requested capabilities and permission-aware interface.
questions.recommendedChoice: Responsive authenticated staff application for patient records, appointment calendar, reminders, assessments, treatment plans, packages, billing, PDF documents, reports, and search; expose controls only when the signed-in user's permissions allow them.

questions.question: Which language should the clinic API use?
questions.rationale: ASP.NET Core has mature authentication and authorization primitives suited to server-enforced RBAC.

options.label: C# (.NET)
options.description: Typed, mature web API and identity ecosystem.

options.label: TypeScript (Node.js)
options.description: JavaScript runtime with a TypeScript API.

questions.question: Which backend framework should be used?
questions.rationale: Pairs with the inferred C# language and supports centralized server-side permission checks.

options.label: ASP.NET Core Web API
options.description: Modern .NET API framework with authentication and authorization support.

options.label: FastAPI
options.description: Python API framework with OpenAPI support.

questions.question: What must the backend enforce and provide?
questions.answer: Persist patients, appointments, clinical assessments, treatment plans, packages, invoices, generated PDFs, and audit events. Enforce Admin-managed fine-grained roles and permissions on every protected API operation. Implement secure authentication/session expiry, appointment reminder scheduling, reporting/search, and documented backup/export workflows. Local development should work with local PostgreSQL and local file storage; hosted email/SMS delivery, cloud object storage, payment processing, and managed backups require provider configuration and credentials and are not assumed active.
questions.rationale: Preserves the requested security and persistence requirements while distinguishing local capabilities from external integrations.
questions.recommendedChoice: Persist patients, appointments, clinical assessments, treatment plans, packages, invoices, generated PDFs, and audit events. Enforce Admin-managed fine-grained roles and permissions on every protected API operation. Implement secure authentication/session expiry, appointment reminder scheduling, reporting/search, and documented backup/export workflows. Local development should work with local PostgreSQL and local file storage; hosted email/SMS delivery, cloud object storage, payment processing, and managed backups require provider configuration and credentials and are not assumed active.

questions.question: Which data stores are required?
questions.rationale: PostgreSQL supports the relational domain; Blob Storage is included for PDF documents, with a local filesystem option for development.

options.label: PostgreSQL
options.description: Relational storage for clinic, scheduling, billing, role, and audit data.

options.label: Blob Storage
options.description: Store generated and uploaded PDF documents; use local file storage during local development.

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: Use only when no persistent database, file store, queue, or cache is needed.

questions.question: Do users need to sign in to use the application?
questions.rationale: Admin-managed RBAC and protected clinic records require authenticated staff access.

options.label: Yes
options.description: Require authenticated staff access and enforce permissions on the server.
